newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish long bond yields end lower, crown firms.
newsitem.headline: Swedish long bond yields end lower, crown firms.

text.p: Swedish long bond yields ended lower on Tuesday, bucking negative U.S. and German trends, and the crown strengthened against the mark.

Dealers said the unexpectedly strong showing by left wing parties in the first round of French parliamentary elections could have benefited high-yield countries such as Sweden because the left wing wants a broad economic and monetary union (EMU).

Players were awaiting the second round of the French elections on June 1 and Sweden's Social Democratic government's announcement about its view on EMU membership. The latter might be announced on May 30 or June 18, a top party official said.
"The liquidity is poor and trade very cautious ahead of the Social Democrats' announcement," a trader said.
The six-month T-bill rate was flat at 4.26 percent and the ten-year bond yield fell six basis points to 7.04 percent.
The crown firmed to 4.4920 against the mark from 4.5115 late on Monday.
"We saw some commercial flows early this morning when some Swedish industrial companies sold currencies for crowns. But since then it has been very quiet around the 4.50 level," a dealer said.
